zh.html.what.title: 这是什么
zh.html.what.p1: IdentityMD（$IMD） 是一个以太坊上的代币。协议自己开了一个 Uniswap v4 交易池，并给它挂了一个自动程序（hook）。这个程序做的事是：池子里囤的 IMD 一旦超过某个数量，超出的部分就会被抽走并销毁——其中 85% 永久销毁，15% 分给质押者。
zh.html.what.p2: 这个机制让 IMD 持续通缩，也是质押收益的来源。所以「它还在不在工作」直接关系到持币者与质押者。
zh.html.what.p3: 这个页面回答两个问题：烧毁还在工作吗？如果停了，还差多少 IMD 才会重新开始？
zh.html.what.quoteLabel: 设计意图 · 来自项目方的链上留言
zh.html.what.quote1Note: 也就是说：这个 hook 在有人抛售时低价买入 IMD，烧掉 85%，把剩下的分给长期持有者。结果是质押者赚到奖励、长期持有者的份额随时间变大——双向激励。
zh.html.what.quote2Note: 它不只为 IMD 存在：已有多个已上线代币（部分市值更高）联系想用这个 hook，项目方正在把它做成可被其他代币复用的组件。这也解释了为什么部署器（CappedBurnLauncher）是无许可的——任何人都能拿它开一个自己的烧毁池。
zh.html.what.readonly: 数据全部从以太坊和 Base 链上直接读取（只读调用，不连接钱包、不签名、不发交易），每 60 秒刷新一次。每个数字旁边的 i 标记点开可以看到它来自哪个合约、哪个函数。读不到的数据会明确写「取不到」并说明原因，而不是显示 0。

zh.html.sim.techSummary: 给技术读者的细节：模拟器的数学依据与已知简化
zh.html.sim.techBody:
held = L × (sqrtP − sqrtP_lower) / 2^96（L339-341，向下取整）；触发线下调 newCap = max(cap − (cap−held)·ratchetBps/10000, cap − capDecay·elapsed/86400, capFloor)（L963-969）；抽走量 floor(L × excess / held)（L997），拆分 rewarded = floor(removed × rewardShareBps / 10000)（L1033-1034）。
已知简化：不复现 AMM 的滑点与手续费；不预测价格（价格是输入）；「净流入」在真实池子里是交易的结果，不是可以独立设定的量。
该模型已用真实历史抽走事件做过端到端复现：算出的抽走流动性与链上事件逐 wei 相同。

zh.html.rewards.techBody:

zh.html.howto.summary: 教程：怎么给项目方发一条链上留言
zh.html.howto.intro: 除了推特和文档，项目方也会读发到这个地址的链上留言——任何人都能发，不需要许可，也不需要持有 IMD。下面是完整步骤。
zh.html.howto.step1: 先写好要说的话。只能发纯文本（UTF-8），会被永久、公开地记在以太坊上。不要写任何隐私信息——私钥、助记词、邮箱、真实身份，一旦上链就撤不回来。
zh.html.howto.step2: 在钱包里发起一笔普通转账。收款地址 0x200E710aCAA6A93bbc77146026328C40F1d60fB1金额填 0 ETH——这个地址是项目方的普通钱包，转 ETH 等于直接送钱，留言并不需要它。网络必须是 Ethereum 主网（chainId 1）。
zh.html.howto.step3: 把文字填进「Hex data / 十六进制数据」字段。多数钱包把它放在高级选项里（MetaMask 叫 Hex data，Rabby 叫 Data）。填进去的是文字的十六进制，下面这个小工具可以帮你转——它只在你的浏览器里算，不联网、不上传。
zh.html.howto.step4: 确认并发送，gas 自付。以太坊主网一笔大约几美元。发出后约一分钟，这条留言就会出现在本页上面的列表里（本页每 60 秒重新读取一次链上数据）。
zh.html.howto.warn: 发之前想清楚三件事：留言是公开且永久的，任何人都能读到、且无法删除；你的发送地址会被一起记录，所以请用你愿意公开的地址；本页只是读取这些留言，不代发、不托管、不收费——别把私钥交给任何自称能代发的人。

en.html.sum.riskTitle: One more thing you should know
en.html.sum.jump: ↓ Everything below is the evidence and mechanism detail, and every item can be opened up and checked
en.html.what.title: What this is
en.html.what.p1: IdentityMD ($IMD) is a token on Ethereum. The protocol opened its own Uniswap v4 pool and attached an automatic program (a hook) to it. What that program does is this: once the IMD sitting in the pool passes a certain amount, the excess is pulled out and destroyed — 85% of it burned permanently and 15% distributed to stakers.
en.html.what.p2: That mechanism keeps IMD deflationary, and it is where staking yield comes from. So whether it is still running matters directly to holders and stakers.
en.html.what.p3: This page answers two questions: is the burning still working? And if it has stopped, how much more IMD is needed before it restarts?
en.html.what.quoteLabel: Design intent · from the team's on-chain messages
en.html.what.quote1Note: In other words: when people are selling, the hook buys IMD cheap, burns 85% of it and hands the rest to long-term holders. The result is that stakers earn rewards while long-term holders' share of the network grows over time — a double incentive.
en.html.what.quote2Note: It does not exist for IMD alone: several live tokens (some with a higher market cap) have asked to use this hook, and the team is turning it into a component other tokens can reuse. That also explains why the launcher (CappedBurnLauncher) is permissionless — anyone can use it to open a burn pool of their own.
en.html.what.readonly: Every number is read straight from Ethereum and Base (read-only calls: no wallet, no signing, no transactions) and refreshed every 60 seconds. The i next to a figure opens up the contract and the function it came from. Anything that cannot be read says “unavailable” and explains why, instead of showing a 0.

en.html.doors.lede1: What this means: even if the first door recovers, destruction will not happen on its own — the second door needs someone to pay gas and call it on Base.

en.html.sim.techSummary: Details for technical readers: the maths behind the simulator and its known simplifications
en.html.sim.techBody:
held = L × (sqrtP − sqrtP_lower) / 2^96 (L339-341, rounded down); the trigger line decays as newCap = max(cap − (cap−held)·ratchetBps/10000, cap − capDecay·elapsed/86400, capFloor) (L963-969); the amount pulled out is floor(L × excess / held) (L997), split into rewarded = floor(removed × rewardShareBps / 10000) (L1033-1034).
Known simplifications: the model does not reproduce AMM slippage or fees; it does not predict price (price is an input); and “net inflow” is an outcome of trading in a real pool, not something that can be set independently.
The model has been reproduced end-to-end against real historical trim events: the liquidity it computes matches the on-chain event wei for wei.
en.html.trimnow.title: How much would burn if it triggered right now
en.html.trimnow.note: A note on rounding: every pull-out rounds down on its own, so adding up rewards / total across all historical trims gives 1499 bps rather than the configured 1500 bps. A single split is exactly 1500 bps. The owner has not changed the rate.
en.html.rewards.title: Why staking rewards are zero
en.html.rewards.lede: What this means: with burning stopped, the 15% that goes to stakers has stopped with it. The money in the two buckets below sits there by design rather than by accident — but it can be taken out by the owner.
en.html.rewards.techSummary: Details for technical readers: the three buckets and why the funds stay put
en.html.rewards.techBody:
RewardDistributor splits rewards into three buckets by stakingBps / bondingBps / nftBps. The source comment reads “Only the staking bucket is routed today”; the bonding and NFT buckets are bookkeeping only, to be moved later with emergencyWithdraw() (L92-99). There is no such switch as BONDING_LIVE in the source.
The owner of RewardDripper can call rescueERC20() (L178-181) to withdraw the entire reward buffer.

en.html.simd.lede: What this means: the redemption rate below is not your yield. Almost all of it was set by a one-off operation when the vault was first deployed, and it has nothing to do with staking rewards.

en.html.howto.summary: Tutorial: how to post an on-chain message
en.html.howto.intro: Beyond Twitter and the docs site, the team also reads the on-chain messages sent to this address — anyone can post, no permission needed and no IMD required. Here is the whole procedure.
en.html.howto.step1: Write what you want to say first. Plain UTF-8 text only — it is recorded on Ethereum permanently and publicly. Never include anything private: a key, a seed phrase, an email address, your real name. Once it is on-chain it cannot be taken back.
en.html.howto.step2: Start an ordinary transfer in your wallet.Recipient 0x200E710aCAA6A93bbc77146026328C40F1d60fB1Set the amount to 0 ETH — this address is the dev's plain wallet, so ETH sent here is a gift, not a requirement. The network must be Ethereum mainnet (chainId 1).
en.html.howto.step3: Put the text into the "Hex data" field. Most wallets hide it under advanced options (MetaMask calls it Hex data, Rabby calls it Data). What goes in is the text encoded as hex — the converter below does that for you, in your browser only. Nothing is uploaded.
en.html.howto.step4: Confirm and send; you pay the gas. Roughly a few dollars on Ethereum mainnet. About a minute later the message shows up in the list above — this page re-reads the chain every 60 seconds.
en.html.howto.warn: Three things to settle before you send: messages are public and permanent — anyone can read them and nobody can delete them; your sender address is recorded alongside it, so use an address you are happy to have public; this page only reads these messages — it never posts for you, never holds funds, never charges a fee. Do not hand a private key to anyone who claims they will post it for you.
